resolvedFailures: Initial test launch needed explicit /app working directory and the existing development-dependency cache mount; cleanup succeeded.

ESLint required explicit null/undefined equality; corrected without weakening tests.
TypeScript required explicit JSDoc at untrusted payload and Express error-handler boundaries; added annotations.
skippedAndLimits: The unrelated application-wide suites were not run; the complete affected customer regression suite was run with zero new failures.
No production data or live NetSuite records were used. NetSuite runtime is verified through a SuiteScript VM boundary harness and official API documentation, not an installed NetSuite deployment.
Coverage excludes the VM-executed sender and the one-line server registration; sender behavior and actual full-server routing are tested separately.
The default settings callback is exercised by the real application smoke test outside the measured unit/integration coverage run.
Six normalizer branches are not covered by the focused coverage run; no claim of exhaustive hostile-input coverage.
No dependency audit or migration rollback rehearsal was needed: dependency versions and database schema were unchanged.
No UI browser test was needed: the existing customer searches are used without UI changes.
Random test-file order was not added; deterministic property seeds, serial file execution and concurrency-specific tests were used.
NetSuite delivery has no durable retry queue; failed delivery is logged and the customer can be saved again.
Hard deletes and removed child-address/contact propagation are outside this change.
